feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR National News for reporting across the United States. Explore coverage of economic affordability, immigration, climate, environmental policy, justice and social trends.

entry.title: Four Corners region faces flood threat after days of heavy rain
entry.summary: The area where four states meet in the U.S. Southwest remains on a flood watch after days of heavy rain and winds.

entry.title: How AI is transforming hurricane forecasts
entry.summary: Hurricane forecasters are increasingly using artificial intelligence to make predictions.

entry.title: Court ruling fails to end wait for thousands of immigrants stuck abroad without visas
entry.summary: A federal judge struck down a Trump administration ban on issuing immigrant visas to people from 75 countries, but immigrants continue to be stuck in their countries.

entry.title: Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them
entry.summary: Republicans redrew Congressional district lines to try to tilt the midterms in their favor. But now they are facing expensive and competitive races they had hoped to outmaneuver.

entry.title: Loggers say Roadless Rule repeal won't solve their biggest challenges
entry.summary: President Trump is planning to open up some of the nation's last pristine forests to road building and timber companies. But those who work in the woods say it won't do enough to revive the industry.

entry.title: An inside look of the massive data center tearing a Wisconsin community apart
entry.summary: In Port Washington, Wisconsin, there's a data center being built that's as big as 500 football fields. Residents aren't sure if it could save their community or destroy it.

entry.title: New Colorado library helps people check out nature, not just books.
entry.summary: A new library in Colorado helps people check out nature, not just books. Library cards give free access to camping gear, nature trails and outdoor experiences.

entry.title: Horror fans on the movies that still scare them
entry.summary: NPR's Brianna Scott and Gabriel Sanchez explain why they love the films that scare them, and have some tips for Halloween watching.

entry.title: Why Wisconsin's tight governor's race matters
entry.summary: The close race for governor in Wisconsin is being watched to see how a candidate back by President Trump does in a state where rural voters have sometimes swung from one party the other.

entry.title: Big name campaign surrogates make final overtures to voters as Election Day nears
entry.summary: With high profile visits from President Trump, Vice President Vance, former President Barack Obama and former Vice President Kamala Harris, the spotlight is on campaign surrogates in the final days before Election Day.
